overview.title: TC3 UnitTest documentation
overview.introduction:
TC3 UnitTest is a testing framework for TwinCAT 3 PLC applications. Your tests execute in the TwinCAT runtime, alongside the logic they exercise. The library provides common execution lifecycles, result handling and diagnostic events; a separate PC runner evaluates the reported outcomes.

You define the scenario, resource bindings, stimuli and expected behavior. Test Cases contain the individual scenarios, Test Suites group them, and Run Control coordinates the run. Preparations establish a starting condition when needed, while Assertions check the observed behavior.

This reference is for PLC developers using the supplied library and authors extending its base function blocks. Start with a functional area to understand related elements, or browse by element type when you already know whether you need a block, a data type or an interface. Detail pages describe inputs, properties, methods and protected extension points, including inherited members and their origins.

sections.heading: Using this help
sections.text: Use the catalog filters to narrow the reference by name or purpose, functional area and element type. The navigation follows your current type rather than listing every member of the library. Class diagrams show inheritance and implemented interfaces; field and member tables lead to the detailed declarations. Full-text search also finds terms in parameter descriptions.

sections.heading: Getting started
sections.text: Start with the Authoring Guide for installation and library parameters, then implement your test elements and connect the cyclic application. Choose the compiled library for regular installation or the source-visible alternative with the same identity. Use the help from the matching release; parameter pages show library defaults rather than a consuming project's overrides.

sections.heading: Reference scope
sections.text: This reference includes public framework declarations, protected extension points and the types required by their signatures. Required internal types retain their source visibility and are identified on their pages. Private implementation members, runtime composition and SelfTests are excluded. The automatically generated version declaration is checked as metadata and presented on About and license.
